Above the circle there is a horizontal tangent TP, the point of tangency is T, and TP is labeled 4; below the circle there is a horizontal tangent T'Q parallel to it, the point of tangency is T', and T'Q is labeled 9. On the right side there is a slanted tangent passing through P, T'', Q, and the point of tangency is T''. Reasoning: From the same external point, the two tangents drawn to a circle have equal tangent segment lengths. Therefore, starting from point P, PT''=PT=4; starting from point Q, QT''=QT'=9. So the hypotenuse PQ=PT''+T''Q=4+9=13. The vertical distance between the two horizontal tangents is equal to the diameter of the circle, namely 2r. Because T and T' are points of tangency on parallel horizontal tangents and are located at the two ends of the same diameter, the horizontal displacement of P and Q is T'Q-TP=9-4=5. Thus the two legs of the right triangle with PQ as hypotenuse are 2r and 5, so (2r)^2+5^2=13^2. Solving gives 4r^2+25=169, 4r^2=144, r=6.
